title: A Cipher for the Cover
premise: Rafael Kavanagh, a disgraced intelligence analyst hiding in a coastal border town, is approached by a stranger named Ilsa who claims Rafael saved her life in Prague—an event Rafael has no memory of. Ilsa's 'interest' is a debt of loyalty: evidence that a cargo convoy scheduled to pass through the local checkpoint during a shift change is carrying a device meant to detonate as a 'gas accident.' As Rafael digs in, she discovers the debt is real in a way she never expected—the incident that ended her career was engineered to erase her knowledge of this exact operation, and the man who burned her is running the plot. Rallying a found family of misfit locals and one honest border officer she falls for, Rafael must expose the attack before the shift change, ending with the convoy stopped, her record quietly restored, and a life she finally chooses rather than hides in.
about_author: Rafael Montrose is a former logistics consultant who spent a decade near border towns before turning to fiction full-time. He writes thrillers about people the system discarded who refuse to stay discarded.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Rafael Kavanagh's POV. Three years after being fired, Rafael works nights at a marina office, sleeping four hours at best. A woman, Ilsa, appears with a file and a claim: Rafael saved her in Prague. Rafael remembers nothing. The emotional beat is wary unease—the first crack in her carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Ilsa explains she's repaying a debt with intelligence: a convoy will pass the Corren checkpoint at shift change, and it will be recorded as an industrial gas accident. Rafael dismisses her as unstable—until Ilsa cites a classified routing detail only someone inside would know. Beat: reluctant curiosity overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: Four Hours of Sleep
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, with a flashback to the incident. Insomnia tightens as Rafael runs Ilsa's claims against old habits she swore she'd abandoned. A flashback shows the night her career ended—a report she can't fully recall writing. Beat: the past isn't past; it's waiting.

chapters.title: The Man at the Marina
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A well-dressed stranger, Mr. Voss, buys fuel he doesn't need and asks pointed questions about new faces in town. Rafael recognizes the interview style: she used to conduct it. Someone is looking for Ilsa—or for her. Beat: hunted without proof of being hunted.

chapters.title: Debt of a Dead Language
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa's chapter reveals Prague: a safehouse, an analyst who flagged a convoy and was discredited before the attack she predicted was quietly rerouted. Ilsa owes her life to that warning. Beat: Ilsa's guilt and devotion, and the reveal that Rafael's 'incident' was the erasure.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Corren
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael cases the checkpoint under the pretext of a marina delivery and meets Deputy Officer Tomas Reyes, who notices her noticing. Their sparring is electric; he's the first person in years to look at her directly. Beat: connection as risk.

chapters.title: The Report She Can't Remember
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Digging through a storage unit, Rafael finds her own Prague draft—pages proving she predicted the convoy op and was burned to bury it. Her insomnia finally makes sense. Beat: grief and fury braided together; she wasn't broken, she was deleted.

chapters.title: Found Family, Bad Tradecraft
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael recruits her ragtag circle: Dez, a teenage drone hobbyist; Marisol, a diner owner with a scanner hobby; and grudgingly, Ilsa. Their first surveillance op is chaotic but yields the convoy's false manifest. Beat: warmth and comedy—she has a team again, and it terrifies her.

chapters.title: Voss Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Voss corners Rafael: come back to the agency, records restored, if she hands over Ilsa and forgets Corren. He dangles the one thing she wants—her name cleared. Beat: temptation sharpened by the memory of who did the burning.

chapters.title: What Tomas Saw
chapters.summary: Tomas Reyes's POV. Tomas reviews checkpoint anomalies—a maintenance order that predates its own paperwork—and realizes the shift change is being manipulated. He doesn't know for what, but he knows Rafael is circling the same wound. Beat: duty pulling him toward her.

chapters.title: The Prague File
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa confesses the full truth: her brother died in the original convoy 'accident,' and she's spent years finding the analyst who tried to stop it. The debt was never abstract. Beat: grief made purpose; Rafael and Ilsa's alliance becomes something like sisterhood.

chapters.title: Gas, On Paper
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The team reconstructs the plan: a tanker of industrial solvent, a timed breach, a plume over the checkpoint town blamed on a valve failure. The casualty modeling is cold, bureaucratic, familiar—Rafael wrote models like it. Beat: horror at recognizing the author's hand; Voss's fingerprints.

chapters.title: Three Days to Shift Change
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. With 72 hours left, Rafael weighs Voss's offer against the town she's quietly come to love. Marisol feeds her; Dez fixes her laptop; Tomas brings her coffee and no questions. Beat: the found family becomes the reason, not the complication.

chapters.title: The Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Voss, impatient, leaks Rafael's location to old enemies and has Dez's drone traced. A break-in at the marina office; Rafael escapes through muscle memory she didn't know she kept. Beat: the cost of staying invisible revealed—there is no invisible anymore.

chapters.title: Confession at the Diner
chapters.summary: Rafael and Tomas, dual POV. Rafael tells Tomas everything over closing-time coffee, expecting him to report her. Instead he brings the maintenance order. Beat: love declared in the currency of trust—evidence handed over, not a kiss.

chapters.title: The Insider
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas identifies the checkpoint insider coordinating the shift change: his own supervisor, a man who taught him the job. Betrayal cuts both ways as Tomas realizes his loyalty has been a cover all along. Beat: disillusionment and resolve.

chapters.title: Twenty Hours
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The plan crystallizes: swap the convoy's routing flag, force an inspection, and get the solvent manifest to a federal contact Ilsa trusts—before the shift change seals the window. Everything must go right once. Beat: taut preparation, quiet dread, the team at its best.

chapters.title: The Debt Called In
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Voss takes Ilsa, trading her to force Rafael's silence. Ilsa, expecting capture, has already hidden the key evidence with Dez. Beat: sacrifice as repayment—the debt paid in full, and Rafael refusing to let it be enough.

chapters.title: Checkpoint, Zero Hour
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Climax begins: Rafael walks into the checkpoint during the shift change with the forged routing flag while Tomas stalls his supervisor. Voss arrives with Ilsa. The tanker is minutes out. Beat: all threads converge; Rafael chooses the open door over the safe one.

chapters.title: What the Plume Would Have Been
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, climax. Rafael confronts Voss publicly, playing back his own words on the checkpoint PA as federal contact agents move in; Tomas arrests his supervisor; the tanker is diverted to inspection. Voss offers her old life one last time. She declines. Beat: catharsis—the analyst who was deleted deletes him.

chapters.title: Sleeping Through the Night
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Aftermath: the 'gas accident' never happens, the record is quietly corrected, and Rafael is offered reinstatement. She sleeps eight hours for the first time in three years—and wakes to Tomas knocking with coffee and no agenda. Beat: release; grief finally has somewhere to go.

chapters.title: A Cipher for the Cover
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, coda. Weeks later, Rafael stays in Corren—consulting, teaching Dez tradecraft, eating at Marisol's. Ilsa, free of her debt, stays too. Rafael finally decodes the last cipher: her cover name was never hiding who she was, only delaying when she'd claim it. Beat: belonging, chosen and earned.
